Create a survival and competing-risk report

Source: R/cifreport.R
cifreport.Rd

Create a survival and competing-risk report

Usage

cifreport(
  data,
  outcomes,
  exposure,
  characteristics = character(),
  time.point = NULL,
  subset.condition = NULL,
  filename.cifreport = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  overall = FALSE,
  conf.int = 0.95,
  table1.args = list(),
  code.exposure.ref = NULL,
  data.name = NULL,
  subgroup = NULL,
  label.strata = NULL,
  order.strata = NULL,
  level.strata = NULL,
  outcome.type = NULL,
  cifplot.args = list(),
  output.file = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per subject.

outcomes

A named list of outcome definitions. Each is a list with column names time and event, and optionally outcome.type to override the shared outcome type, code.event1 (default 1), code.event2 (default 2, for competing risks), code.censoring (default 0), and time.point to override the shared time points. Use estimator = "KM" or "1-KM" for survival and "AJ" or "1-AJ" for competing risks. Defaults are "KM" and "AJ". The name of each definition is its outcome label.

exposure

Character vector of grouping column names, or a named list whose entries are column names or lists with variable and optional code.exposure.ref, level.strata, order.strata, and label.strata. Vector or list names identify exposure definitions.

characteristics

Character vector of baseline columns for Table 1.

time.point

Shared numeric evaluation times. May be omitted when each outcome supplies its own times.

subset.condition

One condition defining the analysis population. Use a logical vector, character condition, one-sided formula, or quoted expression. Missing condition values are excluded. NULL includes all rows.

filename.cifreport

One or more paths ending in .docx, .pdf, .html, or .htm. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory. Parent directories must exist. Existing files are overwritten after rendering. If omitted, saves yyyymmdd_<data.name>_analysis_report.docx in the working directory. Supply NULL to return the results without writing any files. Multiple filenames share one analysis. Word output uses editable tables with 9-point text and requires the xml2 and zip packages. PDF requires Chrome, Chromium, or Microsoft Edge. Set the CIFREPORT_BROWSER environment variable to the browser executable if it is not found automatically.

title

Report title. The default is Statistical Analysis Report of <data.name> on <yyyymmdd>.

overall

Include an overall column in Table 1 when there are multiple groups.

conf.int

Pointwise confidence level for the curve and risk ratio.

table1.args

Named list of additional arguments to gtsummary::tbl_summary(), such as label and type. Column label attributes are also supported. Characteristics with a named labels attribute are summarized as categorical using those value labels. When comparison is possible, Table 1 includes p-values from the default tests of gtsummary::add_p() across the observed exposure groups.

code.exposure.ref

Reference level for the risk ratios. Supply one level for all exposures or a named vector/list keyed by exposure section labels. A reference in an exposure definition takes precedence. By default the first observed factor level is the reference.

data.name

Dataset name used in the default filename and title. By default it uses the supplied data object's name, or "data" for an inline expression.

subgroup

Name of one categorical column. In addition to the analysis population as a whole, the report includes each observed level of this column within that population. Missing values contribute only to the analysis population as a whole. Numeric category codes are supported.

label.strata

Display labels, either named by the original exposure codes or given in the order of level.strata. Supply any strata argument as a vector, or as a named list keyed by exposure definition for separate settings. Exposure-specific settings in exposure take precedence. The same labels and order are used in tables and figures. Use original exposure codes for code.exposure.ref.

order.strata

Exposure codes in display order. Codes omitted from this vector follow in their default order.

level.strata

Expected exposure codes. Unnamed labels are matched to these codes by position. If omitted, the levels in the data are used.

outcome.type

Shared outcome type, "survival" or "competing-risk". The default NULL (also "auto") uses the same rule as cifcurve(): more than two observed event codes indicate competing risks. Otherwise the outcome is treated as survival. Detection uses the population selected by subset.condition before splitting into subgroups. Specify "competing-risk" explicitly if an expected event code is absent.

cifplot.args

Named list of cifplot() display arguments shared by all figures. Use the individual arguments for axis labels and scales, legends, confidence bands, risk and estimate tables, event marks, quantiles, and styling. For example, list(label.x = "Months", add.risktable = FALSE, legend.position = "bottom"). Set stratum labels and order through the report's strata arguments. Use add.conf to show or hide the bands and conf.int at report level to set their confidence level. By default the y-axis follows the outcome's estimator. type.y changes the figure's scale only. Competing-event marks use the observed event times for each competing-risk outcome. Settings apply to single-curve figures, with multiple exposure groups overlaid when present.

output.file

Older name for filename.cifreport. Supply only one.

Value

Invisibly, a list with output.file (absolute paths in the order requested, or NULL if no file was saved), specifications, tables, figures, fits, status and versions. Tables, figures and fits are nested by population and grouping definition. Table 1 is a gtsummary object. Tables 2–5 are numeric result data frames with outcome and group identifiers. Group codes and display labels are available in Tables 2–4. Figures and fits are indexed by outcome, with risk-ratio fits indexed by time.

Details

Each population and grouping variable produces a section containing a baseline table, full-follow-up event counts, cumulative counts and probabilities at requested times, crude risk ratios, curve comparison tests, and outcome-specific plots. Observed cumulative counts include events at exactly the requested time. Table 3 and, by default, the figure use the selected estimator scale. Percentages in the tables are displayed to one decimal place by default. KM is survival, 1-KM is event probability, AJ is primary-event cumulative incidence, and 1-AJ is its complement. Probabilities and confidence limits beyond the last observed follow-up in a group are omitted. Risk ratios compare event probabilities (1 minus survival for survival outcomes), with one unadjusted fit per time. Competing-risk fits jointly model both causes. Log-rank and Gray tests compare curves over follow-up. Table titles use the exposure's variable label (label attribute) when available and include its displayed levels when it has value labels. Subgroup titles use the variable and value labels when available. For exposure levels, label.strata takes precedence over the data's value labels. Unlabelled codes are displayed as given. Within a subgroup level, an outcome with zero observed events over the entire follow-up stops after Table 2. For competing risks, this requires zero primary and zero competing events across the exposure groups.

Missing baseline values are summarized by default. Missing group values skip the population/group combination. Missing outcome values skip that outcome within the population. Single-level groups retain descriptive results. A missing reference level affects risk ratios only. The analysis log records invalid, skipped, unsupported and failed analyses and warnings.

The report supports unweighted, right-censored data with one row per subject, one primary event code and, for competing risks, one competing event code. File output requires optional reporting packages and Pandoc. See vignette("v7_reporting_results") for examples and supported configurations.

See also

cifcurve(), cifplot(), polyreg(), ciftest()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("gtsummary", quietly = TRUE) &&
    utils::packageVersion("gtsummary") >= "2.6.1") {
  data(diabetes.complications)
  report <- cifreport(
    diabetes.complications,
    outcomes = list(Retinopathy = list(time = "t", event = "epsilon")),
    exposure = "fruitq1", characteristics = c("age", "sex"),
    time.point = 8, filename.cifreport = NULL
  )
}
